column1: # Deliberate differences between this pack's processors and Yomitan's Russian processors at d3c54c1 (docs/languages.md 8.2), checked by tools/check-yomitan.mjs. Yomitan has no Russian transforms, so there are no rule rows.

column7: Yomitan's yoToE turns every е of the text into ё at once (перенес -> пёрёнёс), which is never a word: a Russian word has at most one ё, its stressed vowel. The pack writes ё for one е at a time (перенёс, from the last е back to the fourth from the start), so for a text with two or more е only the variant with every е changed is Yomitan's alone.
The other side of the row above: for a text with two or more е the pack's variants with one ё (перенёс, перёнес) are not among Yomitan's, which has only the variant with all of them changed.

Yomitan also writes Ё for a capital Е after the first letter (лЕг -> лЁг). The pack's decapitalize processor runs first, so text in capitals reaches yoToE in lower case too (ЛЕГ -> лег -> лёг); a capital Е is changed only as the first letter of a word (Ежов -> Ёжов for names written with ё).
The pack's capital-first-letter variant gives Ё for the first letter of ЕЕ only; Yomitan changes both (ЁЁ, the row above).

Yomitan removes only the acute accent U+0301. The pack also removes the grave accent U+0300, which Wiktionary uses for secondary stress (лѐгкоатлети́ческий), and decomposes first the precomposed Cyrillic letters with an accent (ѐ, ѝ, ѓ, ќ and their capitals) and the combining tone marks U+0340 and U+0341 (canonically the grave and acute accents), so that a stressed text copied from such a source reaches the headword.
